- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.1) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward → reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots → cap forecast at +3–5% above recent high.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (avg 0.0–0.2), model overestimates downward trend → adjust downward by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- Model frequently underestimates mean reversion in 10–14 day horizon → add 1–3% upward bias for 10-day forecast if recent 5-day avg is below 70.
- When sentiment is positive (avg > 0.1) and price is near 75+, model tends to overforecast → reduce forecast by 3–7% for next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is negative and price is near 70+, model often underestimates drop → add 2–5% downward bias for next 3–5 days.
- Model tends to lag sentiment shifts by 1–2 days → adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment turns sharply negative or positive.
